Hmm, it seems another otxo has washed up on our shores.
It's been a few years since the last one.
Let me guess, you found the mask somewhere, you were compelled to put it on, you don't really remember after that...
Then you ended up here, face down in the sand.  Is that right?
It's always the same. You had someone with you as well.
Your beloved, from the looks of it.
They're deep inside the Mansion now, if you intend to find them.
But hold on, don't just go rushing in there yet. You'll be killed instantly.
Let me at least explain how things work around here:
First of all, don't bother trying to leave. You can't.
And don't bother trying to kill yourself either.
You can't truly die while you're wearing the mask. You'll just end up back on this beach.
And you can't release the mask until you've destroyed the heart of the Mansion.
Only then can you be free. Make sense?
Lovely. Now then, why don't we make sure you can handle yourself in there?
Come with me.
The first thing you need to understand is kicking.
The doors in the Mansion are locked, even to your adversaries who patrol it.
You can get them open by kicking them, firing enough into them, or by detonating an explosive nearby.
I'd recommend kicking.  Walk up to the door and deliver a swift kick and it should shatter right open.
Your foes inside the Mansion will be seeking to stop you from progressing.
To that end they'll fire upon you with all manner of weaponry.
Your only recourse is, of course, to shoot back.
You can borrow my old service rifle. Take some shots at these targets.
If you run out of ammo, you can always reload with a fresh magazine.
If you're out of magazines you'll have to find a new gun. Or kick your enemies to death.
This is probably the most important thing I can tell you, so pay attention.
Your adversaries inside the Mansion will have extremely high reaction time.
However, thanks to that mask, you do have a leg-up on them.
You can activate an ability called Focus, which heightens your senses and allows you to move faster than them.
Try activating Focus and slipping your way through the bullets coming from this turret.
You can also roll, which will allow you to dodge bullets as they fly over you.
Alright, just one last thing.
As you kill your enemies, you may notice that you gain a combo meter.
The combo meter goes up if you're killing enemies quickly or in interesting ways.
This is extremely important, especially if you intend to make it to the end:
Enemies will drop more coin if you have a combo going.
If you're going too slowly and not keeping up a combo, they won't drop much at all.
So, for your sake, try to move quickly. Don't be afraid of your foes.
Alright, go ahead and face off against some actual enemies in this next section.
I'll be waiting for you at the end.
Remember, use Focus. It's the only advantage you have.
Well, you're as ready as you're going to be.
Time for the real thing. Good luck. And say hello to the bartender for me.
You have probably noticed a few new faces out here.
We are the servants of the Mansion.
We consist of various wanderers, vagabonds, and transients that have somehow wound up here.
And unlike you otxo, it seems that there is no chance we can ever leave.
Ah, don't worry. We've all made peace with it one way or another.
I suppose I should introduce myself.  I am the Groundskeeper.
I mostly tend to the Mansion's horticulture, but I've become somewhat of a defacto caretaker for all.
Likely because I've been here the longest... well, in a sense.
I get the feeling the bartender and that girl with him have been here much, much longer.
But they seem to be content staying within the Rose Room, so we don't see them often.
Anyways, I won't keep you from your purpose any longer.
Good luck in there, and if you need anything from me, I'll be here.
Ah, trying again, are we Otxo?
I hope your luck is better this time...
You know, we aren't the only ones.
There's beings in there absorbed by the Mansion's power, their minds twisted and weak.
My master is one of them. He taught me everything I know about horticulture...
But there's no saving him now. He's too far gone.
A long time ago, a great hunter arrived on these shores and entered the Mansion.
Unlike others brought to this place unwillingly, it seemed he had come here with intention.
He was a large man of few words but he mentioned something about black saurian-beasts.
He said that he had travelled worlds in order to slay them, that that was his purpose.
Anyways, he never returned to the beach after he entered.
I can't say what happened, but if he's still in there, there's no chance his mind is his own.
Do you believe in ghosts, Otxo?
I know it's a strange question when we're in a place like this.
But I've seen things in the Mansion that don't fit the rules of this world.
Certainly makes a man wonder.
Have you been to the conservatory?
At one time that was my pride and joy, a true melding of man and nature in a handful of beautiful rooms...
Of course my days caring for the conservatory are long gone.
I don't dare enter the Mansion now, lest the husks tear me apart.
You don't sleep.
I know cause I don't either. In fact nobody here does.
Been that way for a long time.
In my time here there hasn't been an otxo quite like you.
You're different... I don't know how, but you're different.
Maybe it's because you still think you can make it. We'll see if that lasts.
Going for it again are we?
Well, here's hoping that you're successful this time.
That bartender is an interesting fellow isn't he?
He's not quite like the rest of us. I think it's because we're not from here.
And I get the impression that maybe he is.
Regardless, he serves a strong drink, so I've got not complaints.
At one point the Mansion used to have a beautiful flower bed surrounding it.
Petunias, marigolds, tulips, orchids, and carnations.
A splendid circle of lillies...
Now it's all I can do to keep the grass at bay and handle the few potted plants.
It's not quite what it once was.
Are you familiar with the lotus flower?
In some cultures it represents the path to enlightenment.
In others, it's the path from death to rebirth in the afterlife.
Lotus grows here, you know. In the ponds in the conservatory.
It's hard to grow much of anything here outside the Mansion.
The salt from the ocean has permeated the soil. Makes it hard for roots to grow strong.
The grass does ok, but it grows in low.
At one time I worked hard to keep the Mansion beautiful...
But those days have long since passed. Now I just do what I'm able.
This ocean is a calm one. No rogue waves, no flooding.
The tide never changes either.
Of course, that's because the time never changes.
Always eternally sunset. Beautiful, eh?
This place never changes much.
It's been a long time since the last otxo, I think we were all starting to get bored.
At least you're someone who hasn't heard me talk before.
Do you grow tired of this otxo?
I did at first... but time continued on, and now I simply exist in a comfortable state.
My purpose is here, to care for the plants and to care for the people.
All it required was some acceptance.
Could I bum a cigarette, Otxo?
Oh sorry, I forgot. Heh.
You know, for a long time I was just here by myself.
Even with the others here, it's quite a pleasure to have your company.
Temporary as it may be.
You know Otxo, I haven't said this to any others, but...
Of all the otxos we've had, I think you're my favorite.
There's something in your eyes. I can't explain it.
But I can see that you're more determined than anyone else.
Sometimes, when the wind is still and the waves are quiet, I sit out here and calm my breathing.
And in that silence, after a time, I can begin to hear a heartbeat that isn't my own.
It sounds like it comes from deep within the Mansion, but who could say...
Have you heard it, Otxo?
You know, I've been in the Mansion a few times, looking for the Master.
But whenever I go inside it's completely empty... except for the bar, of course.
You've met that girl in the bar, yeah?
She's... unusual. A strange girl. Beautiful though.
More beautiful than this Mansion deserves, to be frank.
This Mansion... it needs control, you know?
It fears chaos. You can feel it when you enter.
You seek to shake up that control, don't you Otxo?
I won't lie to you Otxo. Some days I grow tired of this.
The monotony of existing in this place...
But then someone like you comes along and it's suddenly not so drab any longer.
For a time I tried to grow trees around the Mansion, but they never took root.
I don't know if it was just the hard conditions out here or what.
It's a real shame. Some beautiful willows shading the Mansion would be a nice touch.
When I first came here I tended to a bonsai tree.
It was meditative, carefully clipping the branches, shaping it to my desire...
But like all things in the Mansion, it eventually grew brown and hollow, rotted from the inside out.
I did my best to save it but nothing seemed to help.
I never tried to grow another one after that.

Can I help you, sea-wolf?
I'm hard up in a clinch, with no knife to cut the seizing.
I've got to get this dinghy repaired so I can get off this god-forsaken beach.
I don't pay heed to what that blasted groundskeeper says, I'm going to find my way out of here.
Aye, sorry lad. I'm just beginning to forget how long I've been here.
I thought it was only a few weeks ago that I washed up here but... maybe it was months?
What a lubberly soul I've become...
What ocean claims this beach sea-wolf?
I had thought myself a well traveled sailor but alas, I don't recognize these waters.
Is the heading of the sun rise even east...?
This sea isn't like any I've seen.
There's no tides, the waves never change size...
As a man who has trusted the will of the sea his whole life, I find myself lost.
Lad, I can't recall if I arrived in this dinghy or not.
It doesn't look like it's the one from my ship but it's certainly mine now.
If I can just get it fixed, I think I might be able to row away from here.
Oy sea-wolf. Come to hear my moaning again?
Heh, sorry. Haven't got much else to do but complain in my predicament.
I've tried walking the length of the beach, and behind the manor as well...
But every time I end up back here.
So I think the sea has to be the exit. I've tried swimming, of course.
But the waves are just a little too much.  I haven't the strength.
That's why this boat... this dinghy will be my key to get out of here.
Before I was here, I fished every one of the seven seas.
Every season I brought back a plentiful haul.
You ever had a sixteen foot marlin on your line, sea-wolf?
Hell of a fight to bring it in...
How long have we been here sea-wolf?
This eternal sunset muddles the days...
I can't handle the others on this beach.
They've just accepted their predicament. Weak, I say.
But not I. I was raised by the sea! I'm strong of heart and body.
I'll get off this god-forsaken strip of beach if it kills me.
Do you know how I arrived here, sea-wolf?
I was navigating my ship and crew through a brutal night squall.
We'd been sailing for days without provisions. Everyone was tired and ragged.
In a flash of lightning I saw a large rock, a stack. I couldn't believe it.
We weren't that close to land, at least, that's what I had thought.
I tried to turn, but it was too late. We collided.
I can't recall much else, but I awoke gasping for breath on this beach...
That mask you wear...
You can't take it off, can you sea-wolf?
I've heard stories of such a curse in my travels, but never seen it in the flesh...
Oh, Sally Racket, Hi-oh!
Cheerly, man!
Pawned my best jacket, Hi-oh!
Cheerly, man!
And sold pawn the ticket, Hi-oh!
Hehe... just an old tune we used to sing.
Ah! Sea-wolf... sorry, I didn't notice you at first.
My mind wanders when I'm staring out at the sea.
Especially in this place...
Oy...
You... You've been to the lighthouse, haven't ye?
I can see it in your eyes. You've been there for sure.
Hmm...
Here. Let me give you this. It's my old fishing rod.
You seem like you may have a fisherman's eye. Give it a shot.
If you walk up to the edge of the water here, you'll be able to cast your line in.
And if you catch something, you can bring it to the fire over here and cook it.
Nothing beats the taste of fresh caught fish. It's good for the mind and soul.
Oh, you can also only catch one a day. Something to keep in mind.
Despite the utter repugnance of this place, there's life in them waters.
I've seen some fish jumping, and the sea birds are always looking for washed up meals.
Tis a healthy ocean, this one...
Aye sea-wolf... You've caught me wondering if I'll ever be off this beach...
I've got to keep trying, I shan't be stuck here...
You've got a fighter's spirirt haven't ye, sea-wolf?
The way you carry yourself, the look in your eyes.
Knew many a man like you back in my sailing days. Dangerous, they were.
Do ye reckon you're dangerous as well?
Welcome.  What can I get you?
May I interest you in a drink?
I've got the cure for what ails you.  Take a look.
They say a bartender is just a pharmacist with a limited inventory...
What can I get started for you?
Just give me the word and I'll pour you a glass of something strong.

As long as you've got the coin, I've got the drinks.
You look like you've seen better days.  Let's fix that.
What would you like?

And trust me,  you're going to want one.
First one is on the house. What can I get you?
This one's on me.  What can I get you?
Sorry sir, no weapons allowed at the bar.
Weapons are forbidden at the bar sir, please place that somewhere else.

It seems you've done some damage to the Mansion.
Your bill is

coins.

What doesn't kill you makes you stronger. A drink, sir?
Every profound spirit needs a mask. What can I get you?
Without spirits, life would be a mistake, eh?
You've made it this far... You're stronger than you look.
This is the last time I'll serve you. Please, a drink.
You've come a long way. It's my honor to serve you one last time.
Well my friend, this is it. A drink in your honor.
You're almost at the end... One more drink to ease the pain.
Welcome, Otxo.
Do you know why we, the denizens of this place, call your kind otxo?
It means wolf. Because that's what you are... A rabid, violent, helpless beast.
A starving dog only in that condition because you turned your nose at the generous offerings of others.
In short, pathetic.
But it is not my place to judge...
I am a Nun with the Church of Steel, an organization dedicated to the procurement and upkeep of firearms.
As the only apostle of the Church here, the Mansion has granted me some... unique privileges.
Through me you may choose, with some exceptions, what firearms will appear within the Mansion.
Of course, they will be wielded by your enemies. So be aware you may be choosing the firearms that kill you.
And if you acquire any new weapons they too will join the list.
Understand, my child? Good. Speak to me whenever you'd like to adjust your armory.
Let us view your weaponry.
Well well well Otxo.
You've done a fine job collecting weaponry.
The Church of Steel smiles upon such rigorous devotion, and as such have permitted me to grant you a new tool.
The Welwyn .32 will now be yours to use as you please.
Maybe not the most powerful weapon you'll ever encounter... and maybe not the fastest firing...
In fact, some would say it's quite difficult to use indeed.
Regardless! It should be here the next time you stop by. You'll see it in the list.
Blessed be the Church of Steel.
Your armory, acolyte.
Ah my child, the Church of Steel is pleased with your work.
Your weapons...
The Church of Steel welcomes you with open arms.
Your sins will be forgiven my child.
All that matters now is your tools.
Deadliness is next to godliness, as we say.
But ones tools are only as deadly as they are...
Otxo, my child. Please view your weaponry.
Blessings be upon you Otxo.
Your armory awaits.
A devotee to the Church of Steel shall be well equipped.
Please Otxo, gaze upon your tools.
Gunfire is the singing of angels, and the shooter is the conductor of the choir.
Your instruments, my child.
You will die, Otxo. But your are blessed with the gift to choose how.
Heh...
You know, we didn't wish to do wrong.
We were doing what we thought was right. We had to be.
But you... you lead us astray. Not you, but... you know what I mean.
How could we have known the outcome? How could we have known what would happen?
This place, this paradise... it has consumed us. And it continues to consume.
You'll need to speak to the other one. In the motel.
He knows how to get there... if you want to see what we've done.
At long last someone has come to provide me company...
That thing has poisoned my mind. I cannot escape, I will never be free.
It is too late for me. For all of us. We have committed too grave a sin.
I tried to run, but no matter how far I went, I always ended up back here.
Trapped in this room, unable to leave. Unable to die.
I know why you've come to me. You've spoken to the others. You want to see Him.
If... if you stay with me for just a while longer, I'll direct you there.
Please, just a small reprieve from the solace.
Okay... thank you. It is nice to have another living soul here, just for a little while.
When you walk out that door, you'll be in His chamber.
You can see the sin we committed...
So you've made it this far...
I am the master of the Mansion.
I am you.
Maybe you don't remember coming to this place, controlling the Mansion...

THE WRIT OF BEKATUA: Passage 1
In the Time Before, an entity named Bekatua set out to create a home away from the chaos of life.
This was the initial impetus behind the creation of The Mansion.
Bekatua, satisfied with its new home, lived in comfort for millenia.
But that comfort came with boredom, as the doldrums of its unchanging home set in.
There was no surprise, nothing new, because it was simply the world it had created.
So Bekatua decided to test the limits of its ambition in its old age.
THE WRIT OF BEKATUA: Passage 2
Bekatua's plan was to create something its perfect world did not have: chaos.
This would be accomplished with two things. The first: impulse, the need to act.
The second: violence, the need to change.
The first was achieved with Bekatua's creation of The Mask, which would pull entities from other worlds.
That way The Mansion would be populated with new viewpoints and new ideas.
The second was achieved with a device known as The Firearm, which only Bekatua controlled.
THE WRIT OF BEKATUA: Passage 3
Bekatua was immediately pleased with the results of its ambitions.
The Mansion was soon populated with entities from other places and times, who formed a strong community.
Some of them chose to worship Bekatua as a god, others chose to simply live out their lives here.
The Mask did its job dutifully and every new day Bekatua was joyfully surprised.
No longer did the boredom of a perfect world make every day the same.
However, not unlike its creator, The Mask soon became overwhelmed with ambition.
THE WRIT OF BEKATUA: Passage 4
Although The Mask knew and understood the reason for its creation, it felt it could not sit idle.
It could not shake the feeling that maybe there could be more.
It dreamed of a Mansion even greater than this one, larger and more resplendent.
Instead of a small community, a grand city.
A place where Bekatua and The Mask would truly have power.
THE WRIT OF BEKATUA: Passage 5
But when The Mask approached Bekatua, Bekatua's ego would not allow it see its ambitions as worthwhile.
Dejected and ashamed, The Mask instead became devious.
It pulled in more and more entities from the outside, increasing the population of the community.
Soon, as with any growth, the community began infighting.
Every day the strife and anxiety of the community rose, but Bekatua did not know how to keep it in check.
For Bekatua did not see itself as a leader of the community, but simply as a denizen of this place.
THE WRIT OF BEKATUA: Passage 6
The community eventually turned on itself.
Some blamed each other for the issues they were facing.
But a strong contingent began to blame Bekatua, a thought which spread like wildfire.
In a fit of rage the community rose up against Bekatua and cornered it within The Mansion.
Refusing to use The Firearm to defend itself, Bekatua sat idly while the mob whipped itself into a frenzy.
One member of the community eventually snatched The Firearm from Bekatua's hands.
Quickly The Firearm was turned on Bekatua and utilized.
And so, Bekatua was killed.
THE WRIT OF BEKATUA: Passage 7
As soon as Bekatua fell, The Mansion shuddered and became unsteady.
The Heart of the Mansion, the thing keeping this place in existence, was fueled by Bekatua.
Without Bekatua The Heart was soon to die, and it would take The Mansion with it.
The community was scared and immediately regretful for their actions.
However, The Mask had accounted for this, and began implementing its plan.
THE WRIT OF BEKATUA: Passage 8
The mob that had entered in order to face Bekatua turned to The Mask for guidance.
But before they could even ask what they should do, The Mask struck them down.
It was over in just seconds.
Their blood, pooling across the room, soaked into the floorboards of The Mansion.
From the floorboards it then soaked into the arterys of The Heart.
And The Mansion settled.
THE WRIT OF BEKATUA: Passage 9
The community of The Mansion shrank as they were used to fuel The Heart.
The Mask found that it was able to use the corpses of those that had passed as soldiers.
These husks roamed the halls of The Mansion, killing any who entered.
Once the community had been depleted The Mask began travelling outside to collect entities.
Compelled to put on The Mask, they were promised treasure, great luck, or a chance to see a loved one.
THE WRIT OF BEKATUA: Passage 10
The Mask was able to prevent the entities it brought from truly dying, its only power in Bekatua's world.
Even after they had spilled their blood within The Mansion they would wake up back on the beach.
In this way, The Mask could continually milk its captives until they had nothing left to give.
THE WRIT OF BEKATUA: Passage 11
Most of the community died out, with only a handful of stragglers and newcomers remaining.
Those left of the community knew to stay outside of The Mansion.
Meanwhile, The Mask continued to bring in fresh blood to fuel The Heart.
And this is how it has been for some time.
DAY 1
The most difficult thing is remembering how I got here.
I think... I was at the park with my son. He asked me to push him on the swings.
We were walking to the swingset when I saw a mask on the ground...
And some kind of force or something compelled me to pick it up and put it on.
It's hazy, like a dream. I can't quite recall. But I heard my son crying for me, and then I awoke on the beach.
I get the feeling he's inside this mansion. These folks outside have certainly indicated as such.
No matter what, I'm going to get my son back and get out of here. Whatever it takes.
DAY 2
Storming the mansion has so far proved fruitless. As soon as I get in there, I'm shot to pieces.
The pain seems to be extremely real. But as I feel myself fade away, I awake back on the beach.
The things in there don't seem to be entirely human. Maybe once, but not anymore.
I feel no remorse killing them, thankfully. I know they're keeping me from my son.
There's just so many of them. It's difficult to make it deeper in.
All I can do is keep trying...
DAY 3
These people out on the beach are a strange lot.
I feel like they know more than they're letting on, but at the same time, they don't seem to know much.
The groundskeeper in particular seems to have fully accepted that this is his life.
I don't understand it. Don't they want to get out of here? To go back to wherever they came from?
And that nun... I've never met a nun with such an obsession for firearms before.
Strange woman.
DAY 4
This is obvious, but I need to note it down in case I get out of here.
I can't get the mask off.
Try as I might, it simply won't come off. There's no straps, and as far as I can tell it's not glued on.
It just... won't come off. That's all there is to it.
It doesn't restrict my vision at all, so it's not a hindrance when I'm fighting in there.
Furthermore, it seems like it's opaque on the outside, even though it's almost completely translucent inside.
Regardless, I suppose I'm stuck with it.
DAY 5
Despite being here as long as I have, it's occurred to me that I haven't gotten hungry yet.
I don't believe I've gotten thirsty yet either, but I keep buying drinks from that bartender anyway.
And as far as other bodily functions... well, haven't had any of those.
It's like my body is in some kind of stasis. I don't even get tired in the traditional sense.
I say it that way because as time has gone on, I've felt a sort of overall fatigue beginning to set in.
Even though I rest, every time I awake on that beach it's progressed a little more.
DAY 6
Time here seems to progress unusually. Every time I awake on the beach, it seems to be sunset.
Last time, I stayed out on the beach for what felt like hours, just to watch the sun dip below the horizon.
But it never did. It seems this place is eternally almost twilight.
I've been marking the days by the amount times I've awoken on the beach. Even if it's not accurate, it's a decent count.
DAY 7
I haven't written much about The Rose Room.
I kind of cast it off at first, I figured that if I was going to fight, I shouldn't be intoxicated.
But lately I've come to realize the drinks the bartender serves are... unique.
Rather than make me drunk, they make me feel powerful.
Now every time I enter the mansion, I make sure to grab a drink.
As for the bartender himself... he's more of an enigma than anyone else here.
It's like he exists just to serve. I tried asking him questions about the mansion, but he just stared at me.
And that girl in there... I just don't know.
DAY 8
I spent some time today outside of the mansion with the deviant.
I hadn't noticed him at first, but when I finally did, I'm shocked that I didn't.
He's got an unusually shaped skull. Insect like.
Hell, he might be an insect. But he's awfully kind. One of the kindest here.
He's rather obsessed with a collection of... something. I'm not entirely sure what he means.
But he and I have talked at great length about my past life.
He asked me a lot of questions about my son...
DAY 9
My son is in here. I can sense it.
As I get further into the mansion, I can feel that I'm getting closer to him.
But as I get further, there's more to battle through. It only gets harder.
I can't give up.  I can't give up.
DAY 10
I ran into a new figure in the mansion. A man like me, but his mask was red instead of white.
He didn't have much to say that wasn't just downright cruel.
I get the feeling he's like the bartender... maybe a product of this place, rather than a real person.
Still, I don't know what his deal was.
DAY 11
On my last attempt I went through a door that opened to an old arcade, just like the ones I visited as a kid.
It felt strange to be in there. Something didn't feel right.
For a moment I was overjoyed because I wasn't in the mansion any longer.
But the arcade was empty and none of the machines worked.
I remembered my conversations with the deviant. He had spoken about something like this before.
He called them Misplaced Chambers. I guess they're not entirely outside the mansion, but not entirely within it either.
Regardless... besides the strangeness of the room itself, there was an oppressive feeling in my head.
It felt as if I didn't belong there.
I walked out the front doors of the arcade hoping to find a sunny street in front of me.
But I was simply back in the mansion.
DAY 12
I don't know how many of them I've killed at this point.
Hundreds... maybe even thousands?
And yet, it never ceases. I must continue until I've reached the end.
Slowly, but steadily, I am reaching deeper into the mansion.
I can make it. I have to make it. But this fatigue... this damn fatigue...
Every day I'm a little more tired. Weaker. Slower. I need to be fast. I need to be deadly.
I'll finish this, even if I have to crawl.
DAY 13
It appears that at the end of an area within the mansion, I will be forced into a room with a beast of some kind.
There was that mechanical snake at first, but I've been able to handily dispatch that.
But then there was that lizard, or maybe a gecko, made entirely of a black liquid, able to change shape at will.
I don't know what the hell these things are or where they come from, but I suppose it matters not.
They will die, like all the rest, until I've reached my son.
DAY 14
The deviant and I sat together and watched the waves roll in for a while today.
We spoke little, but I get the sense he enjoyed my company.
I wonder, does the continual sunset look different through those compound eyes?
Is it astounding to see it a hundred different times at once?
DAY 15
Over two weeks now. Despite this fatigue, I can feel my skill increasing.
I'm becoming faster, more agile, more accurate. More deadly.
I can consistently get further in. I'm starting to see new areas.
The girl at the bar has rewarded me with new drinks, new powers...
I think, for the first time here, I feel a glimmer of hope.
I can do this. I can reach my son.
DAY 16
I've been thinking about the mask.
Although I was compelled to put it on, I don't feel it exercising any control over me here.
Obviously I still can't remove it. But maybe its power isn't active here?
Every now and then I worry that it will suddenly take control, but at this point I've become confident.
I am in control here. Despite the circumstances that have brought me here, I am all there is.
DAY 17
Today I tried to leave for the first time.
I didn't let myself at first, my goal was only to find my son, and then I would figure the rest out.
But now that I've tried the mansion for some time, I took a look around the exterior.
The beach stretches on for as far as the eye can see.
I tried walking down it, and as soon as the mansion was out of sight behind me, it appeared in front of me.
Behind the mansion is just an endless field of grass.
I tried running out that way, and even though I was continually moving, I never got further from the mansion.
And then there's the sea...
I haven't got a boat, and the few pieces of driftwood on the beach are waterlogged and useless.
So it seems I'm stuck here. Not that I would leave my son behind anyways.
DAY 20
I've skipped a few entries because nothing of note has occurred.
I've been attempting the mansion every day but my earlier thoughts of progress seem to have been with fault.
The further I get the more difficult it becomes.
Deeper in there are new enemies, with different forms and abilities, who are stronger, faster...
Despite becoming more adept I fear that I'm beginning to reach my limit.
DAY 26
I don't even know how deep into the mansion I must go.
It could be infinite, for all I know.
I can feel my son's presence as I push further in, but what if that's just a ruse?
It could be some kind of artificial feeling, it could be this damned mask...
And the worst of it all, I have no choice.
DAY 30
Just about a full month now. The changes to myself have been curious.
At first I was fueled by anger. I would find my son at all costs.
That anger simmered to dedication. I would not give up.
After a time, that dedication turned to despair...
But now I've been overcome with a certain curiosity about it all, which has greatly lifted my mood.
I've had to decide that this endeavor is not impossible first and foremost.
And then from there, I have had to create a strategy.
What weapons do I find most effective? What drinks make me most powerful?
What strategies do I employ when facing certain enemies?
I've been writing down game plan strategies in the sand on the beach. They look like football plays.
The deviant has been watching me, so I've been explaining my plans to him as I draw them out.
He doesn't say much, but he does nod often, which I find reassuring.
DAY 36
So far my planning has proved helpful. I've made it further into the mansion than ever before.
I know what to expect. I move more confidently. My enemies fall before me in a shower of blood.
Each firearm in there is unique, but I have learned the quirks and utility of every single one.
I feel I have to be near the end. The fatigue is stronger than ever before, but I can still shrug it off.
DAY 41
I think that man in the red mask... I think he's related to my mask somehow.
I almost get the feeling the he IS my mask.
Or it's possible that I'm simply going crazy.
DAY 53
I snapped at the deviant today.
He didn't do anything wrong, he was just being his normal self really. I apologized immediately.
But the pressure of this place... I'm so tired and I'm beginning to lose hope.
The exhaustion that I previously mentioned has strengthened to an alarming extreme.
It's making it difficult to make attempts. It affects my speed... my aim...
I'm more reliant than ever on the bartender and his drinks.
But even with them, I don't know how many attempts I have in me.
DAY 59
I think I got close.
I could feel my son so near to me, nearer than ever before.
The room I was in had massive tears in the floor with nothing but space below.
It was almost as if the mansion was starting to tear apart.
Besides my son I could feel something else... like an overwhelming oppressive energy.
But I couldn't reach far enough. I was so close but I couldn't do it.
DAY 68
I saw the man in the red mask again.
He taunts me and me alone. He thinks that I can't do this.
He's getting under my skin... I tried to kill him.
But something wouldn't let me pull the trigger. Not yet. Maybe I saw myself in him?
DAY 74
I've been wondering lately if any of this is real. How could a place like this exist?
But despite any questions of the material, I do know one thing. I am here.
It's not a dream. I hurt, I bleed, I feel.
Whatever this place is, I am trapped here. My son is trapped here.
DAY 80
I've come to accept the conclusion I knew from the start, which is that this is all my fault.
Not just picking up the mask that day in the park... but everything else.
All the hurt I've caused my family. It all rests on my shoulders.
Because I refused to try. I refused to do anything. I was convinced that it was my battle alone.
And now, here in this place, not only have I been unable to save my son...
I've been unable to save myself.
DAY 93
A long time ago I began to love the killing.
At first it was a necessity. If I wanted to see my son, I would have to kill.
I was appalled by the bloodshed and I pulled the trigger by duty alone.
But now I enjoy it. The foes in there don't make any noise, but if they did I imagine I'd like their screams.
Seeing their blood pool on the floor fills me with a sense of glee.
I hate them. So naturally, I love it when they die.
Day 100
This feels like it should be some kind of milestone, but it's not.
In the last few attempts I haven't made much progress.
The fatigue has permanently established itself in my body. I'm weak and getting weaker.
I might be nearing the end of my rope.
DAY 112
My son, if you ever read this, I'm sorry.
This could have all been prevented and it's my fault.
I've tried to get you out of here but I just can't...
I just can't...
DAY 117
I sat with the deviant for a long time today.
I told him of my struggles. He listened, quietly and calmly.
At one point I broke down and began sobbing.
He laid a hand on my shoulder, then leaned in and said that I've done all I can.
Is that it then? I won't get out of here, I won't save my son?
We're doomed to an eternity in this place?
I asked him these questions, and he simply nodded in silence.
I exploded. I struck him and screamed at him.
He couldn't possibly understand what it's like for me. He couldn't possibly understand the pain.
DAY 118
The deviant wouldn't speak to me today. None of them would.
I tried to apologize to him but he simply looked away.
I'm truly alone in this place now. It's just me and the monsters in the mansion.
DAY 127
None of the others will say a word to me.
The only one who speaks to me now is the one in the red mask.
He still chastises me for trying, and now I'm truly wondering why I'm trying at all.
There's no way I can succeed at this point. We're trapped here, we're truly trapped here.
Every day I'm becoming weaker. Soon I won't be able to go on at all.
A bullet will put a hole through my head and I won't wake up on the beach, I know it.
DAY 136
Instead of going into the mansion today, I simply sat in the sand and counted the hours go by.
It was quiet. I'm not sure where the others had gone but I was alone there.
I don't think I can do this anymore.
DAY 138
How long will I have to struggle?
Over four and a half months of struggling. And yet nothing has changed.
In fact, it's only gotten worse. I'm exhausted, the fatigue is killing me.
The others outside the mansion have turned their back on me, which is my fault.
And despite my efforts, I've been completely unable to get further into the mansion.
I think I hit my peak a month or so ago...
It's just not possible anymore.
DAY 145
In a way, I've become at peace with it all.
I've realized that ever since I've arrived here, it's always been impossible.
No matter how hard I would have tried there is no chance I would have made it.
There is simply no route to happiness for me. I am doomed to this.
And with that understanding comes tranquility.
DAY 151
I am more fatigued than I have ever been.
It's a struggle to even lift my rifle, let alone withstand the kick.
I think my time here has come to an end. My next entry will be my last.
DAY 155
I am sure of it now, the next time I die in there will be the last. I won't awake on the beach.
So before I enter the mansion, I want to write a few things.
To my son, I'm sorry to cause you such pain. You deserve better.
I have failed you as a father and as a man. I tried for your sake, but I was not strong enough.
To the others on the beach, I'm sorry for my decorum. I did not treat you all with respect.
The truth is I just cannot take this any longer. The fatigue has left me so weak that I feel death imminent.
I tried so hard, and for so long, and it all amounted to nothing.
I have no choice but to accept that my time has come.
Hopefully a bullet entering my skull will be the last pain I feel.
I am truly, truly sorry.
